proof.text: First prove the boundary-simplex case for every integer $m\geq0$: let $v:(\partial\Delta^m\times\Delta^n)\cup(\Delta^m\times\Lambda_0^n)\to Q$ have equivalence edges on $\{a\}\times[0,1]$ for every vertex $a$ of $\Delta^m$. Here $\partial\Delta^m$ is the union of proper faces and $\partial\Delta^0=\varnothing$. Apply [lem-cbc-initial-prism-horn-filtration] to obtain $X_0\subseteq\cdots\subseteq X_t=\Delta^m\times\Delta^n$ and its horn pushouts. The initial map is $v_0=v$. In this argument $m$ is arbitrary and independent of the fixed $n\geq2$; the initial domain already contains each specified vertical edge, including when $n=2$, because the edge $[0,1]$ lies in $\Lambda_0^n$.

source.place: Lemma 4.4.4.8, proof specialized to the terminal base; finite-prism induction followed by boundary attachment. Relative skeleta replace the source Zorn ordering, using the existing boundary-cell lemma.

proof.text: Inductively suppose $v_{s-1}:X_{s-1}\to Q$ extends $v$. Compose it with the attaching map $\Lambda_{p_s}^{q_s}\to X_{s-1}$. If $0<p_s<q_s$, this horn has a filler by the quasicategory definition in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. If $p_s=0$, the endpoint condition in [lem-cbc-initial-prism-horn-filtration] identifies the attaching initial edge with $\{0\}\times[0,1]$: by the standard-simplex definition, an edge of $\Delta^m\times\Delta^n$ is a pair of monotone maps $[1]\to[m]$ and $[1]\to[n]$, each determined by its two endpoint values. Consequently its image in $Q$ is exactly the original edge $v|_{\{0\}\times[0,1]}$, since that edge belongs to $X_0$ and all previous maps agree there. This is an equivalence by hypothesis, and $q_s\geq2$, so [lem-cbc-equivalence-outer-horn-filling] gives a filler for this outer horn. In either case the filler and $v_{s-1}$ agree on the attaching horn; the stated pushout universal property gives $v_s$ restricting exactly to $v_{s-1}$. Finite induction produces $v_t$ on the entire product. This proves the boundary-simplex extension assertion rather than introducing it as a new lemma node.

proof.text: For the original inclusion $A\subseteq B$, apply [lem-coef-infinity-monomorphism-boundary-cells] to its degreewise injective inclusion. Obtain simplicial subsets $Z_0=A\subseteq Z_1\subseteq\cdots$ with union $B$, where $Z_r\to Z_{r+1}$ is the pushout of boundary inclusions indexed by the nondegenerate $r$-simplices of $B$ outside $A$. Denote the maps supplied by this pushout from its simplex summands by $\tau:\Delta^r\to Z_{r+1}\hookrightarrow B$; commutativity of the pushout square makes each restriction to $\partial\Delta^r$ factor through $Z_r$. Only these attaching maps, not an identification with the indexing simplices, will be used. The degreewise union of the $Z_r$ is a simplicial subset and is itself their colimit: a compatible family of maps defines a map on a simplex by its value in any containing stage, independent of that stage, and the same formula respects all simplicial operators. By the colimit universal property in [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], this union is $B$. Thus every attaching $\tau$ carries $\partial\Delta^r$ into $Z_r$. Construct maps $H_r:Z_r\times\Delta^n\to Q$ extending the prescribed map on $Z_r\times\Lambda_0^n$, with $H_0=h|_{A\times\Delta^n}$, and impose $H_{r+1}|_{Z_r\times\Delta^n}=H_r$. The base case follows because the two restrictions of the given $h$ agree on their intersection.

source.place: Lemma 4.4.4.8, proof specialized to the terminal base; finite-prism induction followed by boundary attachment. Relative skeleta replace the source Zorn ordering, using the existing boundary-cell lemma.

proof.text: Assume $H_r$ constructed. For each attaching simplex $\tau$, its boundary pullback of $H_r$ and its horn pullback of $h$ agree on $\partial\Delta^r\times\Lambda_0^n$. They therefore define a map on $(\partial\Delta^r\times\Delta^n)\cup(\Delta^r\times\Lambda_0^n)$. At a vertex $a$ its initial vertical edge is the specified edge for $b=\tau(a)$ in $B$, hence is an equivalence even if vertices or edges of $\tau$ become identified in $B$. The boundary-simplex argument of steps 1–2 gives an extension $V_\tau:\Delta^r\times\Delta^n\to Q$. Choose one for each simplex in this small set. Glue these maps with $H_r$ using the pushout in [lem-coef-infinity-monomorphism-boundary-cells]. Here is the degreewise pushout presentation directly from its universal property, rather than an appeal to preservation by evaluation. Form a simplicial set $W$ by taking in each degree the disjoint union of the old simplices and the attaching-simplex summands, modulo the boundary identifications; the simplicial operators descend because the attaching boundary maps are simplicial. A compatible pair of maps from the old subcomplex and the attaching summands to any simplicial set $T$ defines exactly one map $W\to T$ by its values on representatives, and this map is simplicial on every summand. Thus $W$ has the defining pushout property and is canonically identified with $Z_{r+1}$ by the unique maps induced in both directions. In degree $k$ this presents $(Z_{r+1})_k$ as the quotient of $(Z_r)_k\amalg\coprod_\tau(\Delta^r)_k$ by the boundary identifications. For each $t\in(\Delta^n)_k$, assign $(z,t)$ the value $(H_r)_k(z,t)$ and $(u,t)$ in the $\tau$ summand the value $(V_\tau)_k(u,t)$. The two values agree on every boundary identification, so they descend to $(Z_{r+1})_k\times(\Delta^n)_k$. All face and degeneracy maps preserve these formulas because the maps being glued are simplicial. This gives $H_{r+1}$ extending $H_r$ and agreeing with $h$ on $Z_{r+1}\times\Lambda_0^n$, since that equality holds on each summand. This spells out product gluing without assuming that $\tau$ is an embedded simplex.

source.place: Lemma 4.4.4.8, proof specialized to the terminal base; finite-prism induction followed by boundary attachment. Relative skeleta replace the source Zorn ordering, using the existing boundary-cell lemma.

proof.text: Induction provides the compatible sequence $H_r$. By [lem-coef-infinity-monomorphism-boundary-cells], every $b\in B_k$ belongs to some $(Z_r)_k$. Set $H_k(b,t)=(H_r)_k(b,t)$ for any such $r$. The extension identities make this independent of $r$ (compare two choices in their larger stage); faces and degeneracies respect this formula since each $Z_r$ is a simplicial subset and each $H_r$ is simplicial. Thus $H:B\times\Delta^n\to Q$ is a simplicial map. It restricts to $h$ on $A\times\Delta^n$ by the base case and on $B\times\Lambda_0^n$ by the stagewise invariant. This is the required extension. Empty $B$, $A=B$, infinitely many cells, and arbitrarily high-dimensional $B$ require no alteration to this construction.

title: Extension of prism horns with invertible vertical edges
statement: Use simplicial sets, horns and equivalences as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Let $Q$ be a quasicategory, $A\subseteq B$ a simplicial subset, and $n\geq2$. Suppose $h:(A\times\Delta^n)\cup(B\times\Lambda_0^n)\to Q$ is a simplicial map such that, for every vertex $b$ of $B$, its restriction to $\{b\}\times[0,1]$ is an equivalence. Then $h$ extends to $B\times\Delta^n$. No finiteness assumption on $B$ or invertibility assumption on its edges is imposed.
